name: Gokarna Town (Temple District)
tagline: The sacred heart of Gokarna, markets and the Mahabaleshwar temple
description: The temple town is Gokarna's original core, a warren of narrow streets around the Mahabaleshwar temple, one of the holiest Shiva shrines on India's west coast. It mixes pilgrim guesthouses, thali joints, provision stores, and the main bus stand. Beach life is a short auto ride away, but this is where you feel Gokarna's identity as a working sacred site rather than a resort.
bestFor: Cultural immersion, budget stays, easy transport links
pros: Central for buses, autos, and shops
Cheapest food and lodging in the area
cons: Modest dress and behavior expected at all times
Can feel crowded and noisy during festivals

name: Gokarna Beach
tagline: The main town beach, walkable and unpretentious
description: Gokarna Beach sits closest to the temple town, a long stretch of sand used by pilgrims for ritual bathing as well as travelers for a swim or sunset walk. It is less developed than Kudle or Om, with fewer shacks, making it a quieter, more local alternative just minutes from the market and bus stand.
bestFor: Quick beach access without leaving town, budget travelers
pros: Walking distance from the temple town
Good sunset views over the bay

name: Kudle Beach
tagline: The most developed travelers' beach, huts and cafes lining the sand
description: A steep footpath or short scooter ride south of the temple town leads to Kudle, Gokarna's busiest beach for travelers. Bamboo huts, yoga shalas, and beach-shack restaurants like Prema line the sand, giving it the fullest range of amenities among Gokarna's beaches while still feeling far calmer than Goa's coast.
bestFor: Longer stays, socializing, yoga and beach-shack work sessions
pros: Widest choice of huts, cafes, and yoga classes
Easiest beach to reach by road
Good sunset viewpoint from the headland
cons: Busiest and most crowded of the beaches
Wifi still unreliable despite more cafes

name: Om Beach
tagline: The iconic OM-shaped beach with the widest range of shacks and boats
description: Named for its distinctive Om-symbol curve, Om Beach is a longstanding favorite with long-running shacks like Namaste Cafe, watersports operators, and boat services out to the more remote Half Moon and Paradise beaches. It has a wider, more scenic stretch of sand than Kudle and a livelier stretch of restaurants and guesthouses.
bestFor: Beach hopping by boat, watersports, longer beach-shack meals
pros: Most scenic beach shape and setting
Boats here connect onward to Half Moon and Paradise
Good spread of shacks and guesthouses
cons: Can get touristy and crowded in peak season
Rip currents make some areas unsafe for swimming
